name: Isosorbide Mononitrate
summary: The active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate with near-complete oral bioavailability, used for long-term angina prophylaxis rather than acute relief.
mechanism: Releases nitric oxide, raising vascular smooth muscle cGMP and causing venodilation (reduced preload) and arterial dilation (reduced afterload), decreasing myocardial oxygen demand.
targets: Vascular smooth muscle guanylate cyclase (via NO)
pharmacodynamics: Sustained antianginal effect with once- or twice-daily dosing; no role in acute angina.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Minimal first-pass; denitration to inactive isosorbide

dosing.adult: Extended-release: 30–60 mg once daily (range up to 120 mg); immediate-release: 20 mg twice daily with a 7 h interval

safety.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed (no adequate data)
warnings: Tolerance with continuous dosing — maintain a nitrate-free interval

clinicalPearls: Not for acute angina relief — onset is too slow; use sublingual nitroglycerin instead.
Once-daily extended-release dosing provides a built-in nitrate-free interval.
good: Patients needing reliable daily angina prophylaxis with simple dosing.
bad: Patients with hypotension or PDE5 inhibitor use; acute chest pain.
